result.note: Tests the registration mandate timeline, policy duration, hybrid exclusion and the central scheme funding charging points in Delhi's June 2026 EV policy.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, the Delhi Cabinet approved a new electric vehicle (EV) policy. Consider the following statements about it:
items: From 1 January 2027, only electric three-wheelers and N1-category trucks will be eligible for new registration in Delhi.
Hybrid vehicles are eligible for purchase subsidies under the policy.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the policy offers no subsidies for hybrids. The INR 150 billion policy takes effect on 1 July 2026, runs until 31 March 2030, and bans new ICE three-wheeler and light commercial truck registrations from January 2027.
questions.source: Only electric three-wheelers and N1-category trucks will be eligible for new registration in Delhi from January 2027.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to Delhi's EV policy approved in June 2026:
items: Electric-only new registration of two-wheelers — from 1 April 2028
School buses — at least 10% of fleet electric within two years
Charging points planned — 32,000 over four years
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: All three pairs match the policy. Delhi's Transport Commissioner said 46% of the city's pollution comes from two-wheelers and three-wheelers and 33% from commercial goods vehicles, which is why the policy targets them.

questions.prompt: Under Delhi's EV policy approved in June 2026, the planned charging points are to be funded by Delhi's own budget and which central scheme?
questions.explain: The city plans 32,000 charging points over four years, funded jointly by the Centre's PM e-Drive scheme and Delhi's budget. The policy also offers scrapping incentives of up to INR 100,000 for owners of BS-IV or older four-wheelers switching to electric.
questions.source: The city plans 32,000 charging points over four years, funded by the Centre's PM e-Drive scheme and Delhi's own budget.
